messages:
alejandro: Heads up — CI started failing premerge SAST for a subset of repos after the RBAC change last night. Errors look like KMS decrypt failures in the scanner worker.

morgan: ugh. seeing the same in prodnightly-run. Is it the scanner service account losing keystore access? :thinking_face:

sre-bot: Alert: scanner-worker-3 failed KMS.Decrypt (permission denied) at 2026-03-23T02:14:12Z. Trace id: 8b2f4c.

kira: I queried audit logs and there are a handful of Deny entries for service-account:scanner@redwood-inference.internal around that timeframe. Looks like a temporary binding change.

alejandro: That matches. We rolled a RBAC change to remove a broad keystore role and replaced it with narrower bindings. Might've missed the scanner SA.

morgan: Ok, so triage: 1) Re-add minimal decrypt binding to scanner SA (temp) 2) Re-run failing CI 3) Backfill evidence for affected PRs 4) Update runbook so this doesn't recur. Agree?

samir: +1. I can do the temp binding and monitor. Which permission exactly? kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt?

kira: On GCP it's cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on the key resource. For AWS it'd be kms:Decrypt. Add only to the specific key used by scanner artifacts.

alejandro: Samir — please do the grant with a short TTL (1h) and post the exact IAM diff here. We'll need to record the change for the audit ticket.

samir: Grant applied with TTL using our ephemeral-grant-tool: `ephemeral-grant create --sa scanner@... --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/scanner/cryptoKeys/artifacts --ttl 1h`

morgan: Thanks. CI triggered a rerun and the SAST jobs are green so far. Repro case: a PR that previously showed 3 findings now completed without KMS errors.

kira: We should mark any findings that were suppressed due to scanning failure as "unknown" and re-evaluate. I spotted 4 PRs that merged with unresolved scanner failures — need to re-open follow-ups if new findings pop up.

alejandro: For the runbook update: add a pre-change checklist that includes a `keystore-access-check` step for any RBAC edits touching keystore roles, run queries against `audit.log` for service principals referenced by CI. Also add an automatic gating check in premerge that validates scanner SA decrypts the key before merging.

samir: I'll draft the runbook change & a small GH action to validate decrypt: snippet below:

```
- name: Verify KMS decrypt for scanner SA
  run: |
    gcloud kms keys versions test-iam-permissions projects/redwood/... --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt
```

morgan: Nice. Also let's add a short incident postmortem note to the security channel and tag infra to review the RBAC rollout tooling — we want a dry-run mode that simulates access checks.

kira: FYI, audit log shows no evidence of exfil or suspicious reads, only Deny for decrypt. So no customer impact expected. Still, we should run quick diffs for any artifact UIDs that failed to decrypt last night.

alejandro: Agreed. Action items: samir — commit runbook PR + GH action; morgan — reopen any PRs with stalled scanner artifacts and verify; kira — run artifact decrypt diff and attach to ticket SEC-2026-314; I'll own the postmortem draft.

samir: On it, sending PR in ~30m. Will also include the ephemeral-grant tool snippet and instructions for TTL.

morgan: I'll scan the last 24h of merge commits for scanner errors and paste a short list.

sre-bot: Deploybot: RBAC change rollout window ended 2026-03-23T01:47:00Z by alejandro. Change id: rb-20260323-17.

kira: small note — consider adding an automated alert that triggers when scanner job fails with KMS.Decrypt more than 3 times in 15m. That would've caught this faster.

alejandro: Good idea. I'll add an SLO/alert ticket. Thanks everyone. Closing thread when PRs + ticket done. :white_check_mark:
